log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Incineroar gives Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot support, and Garchomp is fast with strong Ground and Dragon pressure. Archaludon's Electroshot covers Primarina and Dragonite, which the rest of my team handles less well.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at team preview, I need to pick 3 against their Garchomp, Gholdengo, Incineroar, Primarina, Dragonite, and Kingambit. My side has Incineroar, Garchomp, Gholdengo, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Archaludon, so I'm weighing a core built around Incineroar's intimidate and utility moves alongside Garchomp's speed and typing and Gholdengo's special threat.

I'm checking matchups carefully: their Primarina's Water/Fairy typing threatens Dragon-types with Fairy coverage, while Archaludon's Electroshot and Dragon/Steel bulk could handle Primarina, Dragonite, and dragon attacks well. Kingambit's Dark/Steel profile also looks solid against their Dragonite but is vulnerable to Fighting, Fire, and Ground, which matters since their Incineroar carries Fire coverage.

Weighing these options, I'll settle on bringing Incineroar, Garchomp, and Archaludon for the best overall coverage.

decisions.thought: Incineroar gives Intimidate plus Fake Out and Parting Shot pivot, which is the deciding factor for surviving Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Sinistcha pressure. Dragonite provides speed and Ice Punch plus Earthquake for Garchomp and Archaludon. Primarina covers opposing Incineroar, Garchomp, and Kingambit.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since it's turn one and both sides have Incineroar, Fake Out works well here—it's priority, hits for 40 and flinches the target regardless of speed, since it goes first anyway.

decisions.thought: Priority is the deciding factor here. Fake Out only works on turn one and flinches the mirror Incineroar before it can Parting Shot out.

decisions.thought: Opposing Incineroar is already at -1 Atk, and Parting Shot drops its Atk again while I switch out. Flare Blitz is resisted by their Fire/Dark typing and costs recoil. Garchomp then comes in clean (their Intimidate isn't re-triggered), outspeeds Incineroar at 169 Speed, and Earthquake hits it super effectively.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing means Flare Blitz would only be half-effective against it, and it's already used Fake Out so that threat is gone at full health. I'm weighing my options, possibly including Parting Shot or another move.

Parting Shot would drop their Atk and SpA while letting me switch into Garchomp, which takes only half damage from Fire and outspeeds Incineroar entirely. Garchomp can then hit back with a super-effective Earthquake against Incineroar's Fire typing, and with Parting Shot's stat drops stacked on top, Garchomp should be in great shape to sweep.

decisions.thought: Incineroar mirror has no likely knockout with both at -1 and Flare Blitz resisted. Pivoting out of the stagnant matchup is the deciding factor. Parting Shot debuffs the foe and keeps momentum over a hard switch.

decisions.thought: Only switches are legal, so I need the better lead-in. Garchomp outspeeds the opposing Incineroar's likely range and hits it super effectively with Earthquake, while Archaludon is slower and Fire-weak. Garchomp switching in is the stronger choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I only have switching options available, so I need to pick between Garchomp and Archaludon. The opponent's Incineroar is debuffed at -2 attack and -1 special attack, and since it's Fire/Dark, its Fire-type moves would only deal half damage to Garchomp's Dragon typing but neutral damage to the Ground part.

Archaludon's Steel/Dragon typing means Fire is actually super effective against Steel but resisted by Dragon, netting out to neutral damage from Flare Blitz. Garchomp, however, outspeeds Incineroar significantly and could threaten an Earthquake that hits for 2x effectiveness since Incineroar isn't a Flying type.

Fake Out shouldn't be a concern since Incineroar already used it against a prior Pokemon this turn, so Garchomp should be safe switching in. I'll go with Garchomp.

decisions.thought: Must switch after Parting Shot. Dragonite is immune to Earthquake and faster than Garchomp, so Ice Punch threatens a knockout before it can move.

decisions.thought: Garchomp moves first at 169 Speed, so it can strike before Dragonite acts. Outrage is 2x into Dragonite and never misses, while Earthquake does nothing to a Flying type. Mega Evolving now adds a big Attack boost that will matter for the rest of the game.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp's stats dropped, I'm weighing Stone Edge against Dragonite, which hits super effectively since it's part Flying, versus Outrage, which would only be neutral against the Dragon/Flying typing, while also factoring in Multiscale potentially halving the damage if Dragonite's at full health.

Outrage is 100% accurate but confuses afterward and locks me in; Multiscale halves the first hit unless Dragonite has Inner Focus, and I should move first given our speed. Megaing now uses up a one-time resource, though Mega Garchomp's Outrage hits hard here versus the safer but less reliable 80% Stone Edge, which would let me keep the Mega available for later threats like Gholdengo or Kingambit.

Running the numbers, Stone Edge without mega only lacks STAB and deals modest damage even with a crit, while Outrage without mega roughly halves against Multiscale too. Mega Garchomp's boosted Attack with Outrage looks like the strongest option by far once I account for the stat increase.

Considering the broader matchup against Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Primarina, mega evolving now seems worthwhile since Ground hits Gholdengo hard and Mega Garchomp stays a persistent threat. I'll go with mega Garchomp using Outrage here.

decisions.thought: Garchomp is 4x weak to Ice Punch, so it should be a knockout even without Mega evolving. Staying non-Mega keeps Multiscale at full HP to survive if Garchomp is faster.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is already at -2 SpA, so every special hit is weakened. Dracometeor is the only immediate damage option that can pressure the 56% Incineroar, though its self-drop hurts. Electroshot would spend a charge turn here, and Flash Cannon is resisted by Fire.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Archaludon's stats down and Incineroar at 56% after sitrus, I'm checking the matchup: Electric vs Fire/Dark is neutral damage. Electro Shot normally charges a turn but under rain it hits immediately, boosting Sp. Atk by 1 before the attack.

Draco Meteor would drop Sp. Atk even further despite being neutral damage, and Flash Cannon is resisted by Fire, so it's not very effective. Rough calculations put Draco Meteor around 70 damage against Incineroar's ~113 remaining HP, not enough for a KO, so Electro Shot's charging turn becomes the main concern since it leaves Archaludon exposed.

Dark is neutral against both Dragon and Steel, so that's not a big factor. Switching to our own Incineroar is an option, but Flare Blitz would be resisted by the opponent's Fire typing, and Fake Out alone isn't much pressure. Given Archaludon's SpA is already crashed, Protect won't fix that, so the best play is probably still going for Draco Meteor now while it hits hardest.

Electroshot is tempting since it would boost SpA and offset the drop, but it likely requires a charge turn, giving the opponent's Incineroar a free shot in. With Sitrus already consumed and the opponent at 56%, Draco Meteor would knock them down to around 21%, setting up a finish next turn even with the extra SpA drop.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is faster, but Fake Out has +3 priority so we move first and flinch. This denies damage for free and keeps Incineroar healthy to Parting Shot out next.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Given Archaludon's stats are down with -2 SpA, I'm weighing Electroshot against Incineroar — it's neutral type-wise but weakened by the SpA drop, though it does boost SpA by a stage when it hits.

Draco Meteor is also neutral but similarly halved and drops SpA further, and Flash Cannon isn't very effective here either. With Incineroar at 56% and Fake Out already spent, I'm considering Protect to stall while watching for Parting Shot, and keeping an eye on the benched Dragonite's Ice Punch as a potential threat to Archaludon's Dragon/Steel typing.

With STAB that's roughly 77 damage against Incineroar's 113 HP, not quite lethal, and it tanks our SpA down to -4 which is rough. Electroshot without STAB only does about 52 at -1, also underwhelming. Flash Cannon gets STAB too but gets halved by Incineroar's Fire typing, so I'm weighing all three weak options against each other.

Protect doesn't help our lowered SpA at all, just stalls a turn and risks the opponent Parting Shot to pivot. Electroshot's self-boost timing is ambiguous, but it's our best shot at rebuilding SpA while hitting with perfect accuracy — given Incineroar's healthy HP and our Dragonite option on the bench, I'm leaning toward using Electroshot now rather than Protecting.

Checking Archaludon's stat drops—SPA is down to -2 after the Parting Shot hit—so Electro Shot will be weaker, but it's still neutral against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing at 56% health.

Running the numbers: with -2 SpA, Electro Shot lands around 44-52 damage against Incineroar's roughly 113 HP, so it's not a KO on its own. But Electro Shot charges on the first turn and fires on the second, which matters for timing this exchange.

Dracometeor hits immediately and does get Dragon STAB, bringing it to about 78 damage, but it would tank Archaludon's SpA down to -4 which is brutal going forward. Protect would just stall for info without progressing the game, so despite the risk of eating a Flip Turn or Ice Punch while charging, I'll go with Electro Shot.
